title: WPSS/1682/2020 of BHARAT LAL Vs CENTRAL RECORDS OFFICE INDO TIBETAN BORDER POLICE

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1682 of 2020
Sri Bharat Lal ... Petitioner
Versus
Central Records Office Indo Tibetan Border
Police & Others ... Respondents
Ms. Neelima Mishra Joshi, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
Ms. Monika Pant, Central Government Standing
Counsel, for the respondents.
September 23, 2022
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
By means of this writ petition,
petitioner has sought the following substantive
relief:-
"I. Issue a writ and order or direction
in the nature of mandamus directing
the respondents to give petitioner's
full pension as well as all amount of
petitioner's pension which was not
paid till yet."
2. According to the petitioner, he was
enrolled with Second Vahini of Indo-Tibetan
Border Police in November, 1962, and after
completing more than 22 years service, he took
voluntary retirement on 31.03.1985 due to
health reasons.
3. The grievance raised by petitioner is
that he has been given benefit of general
pension up to 01.01.1996 and thereafter he is
being paid family pension, which is given to
family members after death of a government

2
employee. The averment made in paragraph no.
3 of the writ petition is reproduced below:-
"That it is submitting the petitioner
stating in aforesaid letter that If my
pension is 10150/=Basic then how
much is my family pension. Presently
petitioner's have received pension is
10150/= Basic, 1726/= D.A., 1000/=
Medical allowance total amounting
rupees 12,876/- my account no.
11795031883 should be checked
whether I get family pension or
service, and give all the pension
benefits to the petitioner. Copy of the
letter dated 17.08.2020 is being filed
herewith and marked as Annexure
No.1 to this writ petition."
4. A counter affidavit has been filed by
Mr. Shyam Mehrotra, DIG, CRO, on behalf of
respondent nos. 1, 2 & 3. The stand taken in
the counter affidavit is that service pension of
the petitioner was revised in terms of 5th Central
Pay Commission w.e.f. 01.01.1996 and
petitioner is being paid full service pension and
not family pension. Averments made in
paragraph nos. 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 of the counter
affidavit are extracted below, for ready
reference:-
"4. That the contents of paragraph
No. 2 of the Writ Petition so far as
pertains to Secretary, State Legal
Service Committee, High Court
campus Nainital, Uttarakhand are
denied for want of knowledge rest of
the paras is denied vehemently as the
service pension of the petitioner under
5th CPC was revised by concerned
pension disbursing branch of the
petitioner w.e.f. 01.01.1996 and since
then the petitioner is drawing full
service pension (not family pension) in
his bank account No. 11795031883,
SBI Branch Kaljikhal, Pauri Gharwal,
Uttarakhand. The petitioner, Shri

3
Bharat Lal is in receipt of Pension
revised on the implementation of 7th
Central Pay Commission w.e.f.
1.1.2016 @ Rs. 10,150/- p.m. plus
dearness relief as revised from time to
time and fixed Medical Allowance. He
is not being paid family pension as
stated by him.
The pension revision details of the
petitioner are as under:- Revision of Pension by PAO (ITBP) Revision authorities sent by
CPAO to CPPC of bank
Pension=Rs.3665/-
w.e.f. 01.01.2006 (6th CPC)
Vide pension revision Authority
no. W0231848160900393 dated 25.09.2016
Pension=Rs.3665/-
w.e.f. 01.01.2006 (6th CPC)
Family pension=Rs.3500/- vide
SSA No. 231848500391/1996209/A2
dated 20.10.2016
Pension=Rs. 10,150/- w.e.f. 01.01.2016
(7th CPC Family Pension = Rs. 9000/-
Vide revision authority no. 231848500391A3
Dated 23.12.2017
Pension=Rs. 10,150/- w.e.f. 01.01.2016
(7th CPC) Family Pension = Rs. 9000/-
Vide SSA No. 231848500391/3299457/A3
Dated 12.04.2018
Thus the petitioner is in receipt of
Pension @ Rs. 10,150/- plus Rs.
1726/- (Dearness Relief @17% + Rs.
1000/- (fixed medical allowance)
totaling to Rs. 12,876/- per month. A
true copy of pension revision authority
No. W0231848160900393 dated
25.09.2016, true copy of SSA No.
231848500391/1996209/A2 dated
20.10.2016, true copy of revision
authority no. 231848500391A3 dated
23.12.2017 and true copy of SSA No.
231848500391/3299457/A3 dated
12.04.2018 are being filed herewith
and marked as Annexure No. 1, 2, 3 &
4 to this counter affidavit.
5. That in reply to contents of para no.
3 of the writ petition, it is stated that
it is clearly mentioned in the pension
revision special seal authority dated
12.04.2018 (annexure no. 4 to this
counter affidavit) at SI. No. 7 that
"REVISED FAMILY PENSION AT
NORMAL RATE: Rs. 9000/-". As such
admissible amount of pension and
family pension has been clearly
mentioned separately. The copy of the
authority dated 12.04.2018 was also
sent to the petitioner. The petitioner is
in receipt of Pension @ Rs. 10,150/-
plus Rs. 1726 (Dearness Relief @ 17%

4
+ Rs. 1000/- (fixed medical
allowance) totaling to Rs. 12,876/- per
month. The petitioner is not in receipt
of family pension. It is further to
submit that the disbursement of
Family Pension starts from the date of
next to the date of death of Pensioner.
7. That in reply to contents of para 5
of the writ petition, it is stated that as
per para 4.1 of the DOP & PW OM No.
38/37/2016-P&PW(A)(ii) dated
04.08.2016 and 4 of the DOP&PW OM
No. 38/37/2016-P&PW(A) dated
12.05.2017, in the case of existing
pensioners, the monthly pension
under 7th CPC will be either 50% of
the Notional Pay fixed under 7th CPC
or 2.57 of the existing pension fixed
under 6th CPC, whichever is more
beneficial. In the instant case, Rs.
20,300/- was the Notional Pay fixed
under 7th CPC. The pension of Rs.
10,150/- per month is 50% of the
notional pay of Rs. 20,300/- which is
more beneficial than Rs. 9420/- which
worked out by multiplying the existing
pre-2016 pension of Rs. 3665/- by
2.57. A true copy of OM No.
38/37/2016-P&PW (A) (ii) dated
04.08.2016 and true copy of No.
38/37/2016-P&PW(A) dated
12.05.2017 are being filed herewith
and marked as Annexure No. 5 & 6 to
this counter affidavit.
8. That contents of para no. 6 of the
petition are not admitted as stated. As
mentioned above, the petitioner is in
receipt of Pension and not Family
Pension as authorized/revised from
time to time.
9. That in reply to contents of para 7
& 8 of the petition, it is stated that the
representation of the petitioner has
been replied by the department and
the petitioner is in receipt of his full
service pension and not family
pension. Copies of reply to the

5
representations of the petitioner is
attached as Annexure-7."
5. The averments made in the aforesaid
paragraphs of counter affidavit have not been
specifically denied in the rejoinder affidavit,
however, the stand taken in writ petition that
petitioner is being paid family pension, is
reiterated.
6. The order passed by Revision
Authority for Central Civil Pensions on
12.04.2018 has been enclosed as Annexure-4 to
the counter affidavit. Perusal of the said order
reveals that the pension payable to petitioner
was revised to Rs. 10,150/- w.e.f. 01.01.2016.
7. In paragraph no. 5 of the counter
affidavit, it is stated that petitioner is in receipt
of pension amounting to Rs. 10,150 +
Rs.1,726/- as dearness relief + Rs. 1,000/- as
fixed medical allowance and he is being paid
Rs.12,876/- per month. The amount, which the
family would have received as family pension is
mentioned as Rs. 9,000/- per month.
8. Since the amount, which petitioner is
receiving as pension, is more than the amount
which his family would have received upon his
demise, therefore, the grievance raised by
petitioner in this writ petition appears to be
without any basis. Thus, there is no scope for
interference in the matter.
9. Learned Counsel for the petitioner
submitted that widow of a similarly situate
employee, who retired from ITBP is receiving the

6
same amount as family pension, as is being paid
to petitioner. This, according to learned counsel,
gave rise the suspicion that petitioner is being
paid family pension and not regular pension.
10. When a query was put to learned
counsel for petitioner regarding date of death of
the other person and the amount, which his wife
is getting as family pension, after his death,
learned counsel could not give any satisfactory
reply. In fact, the writ petition is also silent on
this aspect of the matter.
11. In such view of the matter, the writ
petition is dismissed. No order as to costs.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
